jobs.title: Associate Director, Strategy (Demand Gen) (Performance Marketing) (Canada)
jobs.description:
Associate Director, Strategy (Demand Gen)(Performance Marketing) (Canada)

Job Details

Role:
Associate Director, Strategy (Demand Gen)

Department
: Performance

Job Location:
Remote (Canada)

Role Type:
Full-Time, Permanent

Hours:
Monday - Friday 9AM-5PM (in your timezone, flexible hours)

Compensation:
$112,000 - $163,000 CAD + Profit Sharing (after 1 year of employment) + Benefits

Role Availability:
This posting is for an existing vacancy at Thrive Digital

As a company that values inclusion and diversity, Thrive seeks individuals of all backgrounds and experiences to apply for this position. We encourage anybody who is interested in this position to please apply!

About Thrive

Thrive is a leading full-funnel digital marketing agency supporting growth for some of North America’s most ambitious companies. We evolve our services through disciplined learning, continuous improvement, and close partnership with our clients - regularly assessing what works, what doesn’t, and where to raise the bar.

Our mission is to help companies grow sustainably. To do that, we’ve built deep expertise across performance marketing, brand marketing, digital design, and data and measurement, managing more than $5 billion USD in advertising spend over the past decade. Our work spans startups, scale-ups, and enterprise organizations, including Alo, Zoom, Slack, Uber, Asana, Masterclass, Snapchat, Change.org, and lululemon.

Our culture values curiosity, accountability, and thoughtful problem-solving. We challenge our teams to grow and take ownership of their work while respecting boundaries and long-term sustainability. Thrive is a place where experimentation is encouraged, learning is continuous, and people are supported to do high-quality work they’re proud of - together.

The Opportunity

This is a build-and-grow moment. We're expanding our performance practice around demand generation, and the work comes with a portfolio most marketers only get to admire from the outside — think category-defining B2B software and technology brands, the kind of companies whose products you already use and whose growth story is still being written. You won't just be running campaigns for them; you'll be the strategic partner helping them figure out how demand generation compounds into pipeline, market share, and durable growth. That means owning the questions that actually move a business: how do we reach the right buyers earlier, turn intent into qualified pipeline, and build a lead engine that scales as they do? The tactical craft matters — funnel design, lead quality, CPL and lead-to-opportunity performance — but here it's in service of something bigger: shaping how some of the most ambitious brands in tech grow. If your best work has been measured in ROAS, purchases, or app installs, this likely isn't your fit. But if you think about demand gen as a growth strategy, not just a channel, let's chat.

The Role

Joining the Performance department as Associate Director, Strategy, you’ll deliver strategic leadership to performance teams, leveraging industry trends to evolve Thrive’s services and client marketing strategies. You’ll partner closely with leadership to align team goals with company growth, while managing key relationships and ensuring the long-term success of high-complexity, projects and prospects.

Your focus will of responsibilities will be:

Domain:
Recognized as a leader in performance marketing both within Thrive and in the industry, you make expert contributions to the Performance department, ensuring long-term project success and enhancing the skills of those involved.
Client
: Championing client success at Thrive as a leader across large, multi-faceted accounts. Identifying solutions or refining processes across projects and teams to improve client partnerships and client retention.
People:
Manage a team of senior performance marketers and act as an advocate at scale. Helping others elevate their performance marketing skills or add new skills to their toolkit for project growth and performance. You lead a results-driven culture that in turn leads to consistent and measurable growth.
Company:
Support senior leadership in the Performance department and collaborate with other supporting function leaders to develop, set and execute the roadmap for Thrive's short to long-term performance marketing product and services plans.

We’re committed to delivering an exceptional onboarding experience that will create a strong foundation for your launch in this role:

In your first 30 days you’ll
become familiar with Thrive’s tools, processes, and expectations for high-complexity accounts, while building relationships across Performance leadership, strategists, and key cross-functional partners.
In your first 60 days you’ll
begin actively contributing strategic input across high-complexity accounts, supporting key client moments alongside account leaders, and identifying early opportunities to strengthen delivery consistency, team workflow, or performance standards.
In your first 90 days you’ll
step into leading high-impact client moments for high-complexity accounts, demonstrate measurable impact through improved team execution and client outcomes.

Qualifications

You’ve led and owned large-scale, multi-channel, full-funnel demand generation performance marketing programs with monthly media spend exceeding $1M USD, driving sustained performance across platforms (e.g., Meta, Search, YouTube, Programmatic, TikTok).
You’ve led and developed multi-level teams of 15+, including managing managers, setting performance standards, and scaling team impact through others.
You’ve designed and evolved performance reporting and dashboards (using tools like Looker, Google Sheets, Excel, Tableau…) that enable clear decision-making, executive communication, and accountability against business KPIs.
You’ve led initiatives and process improvements adopted at the department or company level, raising performance standards and operational consistency.
You’ve owned performance strategy across diverse business models, leading forecasting, pacing, and measurement while confidently advising senior and C-suite executive stakeholders.
You’ve led complex client relationships with multiple senior executive stakeholders, navigating high-stakes situations and driving buy-in through clear, confident communication and strategic recommendations.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Thrive is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We have zero tolerance for bullying, discrimination, or harassment of any kind, and we strive to create an environment where everyone feels safe, supported, and valued.

This commitment applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, performance management, training, compensation, and advancement. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates participating in any stage of the selection process.

Competitive Total Compensation Package

At Thrive, we offer a competitive total compensation package that reflects role scope, experience, and impact. This includes a comprehensive benefits program with remote-first, flexible work, paid vacation and wellbeing time, career development support, internal career coaches, and robust health, dental, and paramedical coverage, and so much more!

The Use of Artificial Intelligence

Every application, interview, and candidate interaction at Thrive is reviewed and managed by a human. Where AI tools are used to support parts of the hiring process, candidates are informed and asked to provide consent.

Hiring Eligibility by Location

While Thrive operates as a remote-first organization and hires globally, work authorization requirements vary by role and location. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country where the role is based. For roles based in Canada, candidates must already be eligible to work in Canada. Thrive does not provide visa sponsorship.

Beware of Hiring Scams

Thrive Digital will never offer employment or request personal information outside of our official application process. While we do reach out to people on social channels, most commonly LinkedIn, with information about our active job posts, we always include a detailed recruitment package and a link to our careers page to apply. We do not reach out to candidates via text, WhatsApp or telegram or request any personal information. All recruiting communications will come from an @thrivedigital.com email address or our applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).

Thrive is a remote-first company with team members working across multiple regions. We recognize and respect the Indigenous histories of the lands where our team lives and works.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The organization is focused on optimizing operations, enhancing profitability, expanding capabilities, and strengthening its position in a market benefiting from growing demand for greenhouse-grown food production.

The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. This is not a traditional finance leadership position focused solely on stewardship and reporting. It is an opportunity to become a true business partner and strategic leader, influencing critical decisions that will shape the future of the company.

The successful candidate will join at a pivotal point in OP's evolution. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Leadership and Stewardship

The company is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. More than just a technical financial leader, the successful candidate will be a thoughtful and credible executive who fosters trust, accountability, and collaboration across the organization and partners effectively with external stakeholders.
Operationally curious and highly intelligent, with a low-ego leadership style
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity
A builder of high-performing teams and organizational culture
Results-oriented and accountable
An enabler of exceptional data-driven decision making
Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement
An effective and transparent communicator

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a strategic and operational finance executive who enjoys complexity and thrives in a growth-oriented environment. They will bring both financial expertise and a passion for helping businesses improve performance and create value.
CPA designation required.
Proven track record of success as a CFO or senior finance executive within a complex operating environment with a minimum of 15 years, including optimizing and scaling organizations
Accomplished as a strategic business partner, advisor to the CEO and the senior leadership team
Hands-on and strategic capabilities in financial planning, forecasting, cash flow management, and business intelligence, driving operational improvements through financial insights and performance management.
Experience operating in asset-intensive, capital-intensive, or leveraged environments.
Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

Location

The CFO will maintain a meaningful on-site presence and build strong relationships across both operating locations. Regular travel between St. Thomas and Glencoe is expected as part of developing a deep understanding of the business and supporting operational excellence.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join an organization at a defining moment in its journey. Significant investments have been made, the platform for growth is in place, and the leadership team is focused on realizing the full potential of the business. For a finance executive who wants to influence strategy, strengthen operations, develop teams, and help create long-term enterprise value, this role offers both challenge and impact.

If you are energized by building, improving, and leading from the front, we welcome the opportunity to connect.

jobs.title: Director, Financial Services and Technology
Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Director of Finance | Building Products Manufacturer | Mississauga, ON (On-site)

Osborne Financial Search is pleased to be partnering with a privately owned, fast-growing building products manufacturer to recruit a Director of Finance.

The Company

Our client designs and manufactures patented, engineered building products for basement finishing, home renovation, new construction and structural repair. Its products include market-leading brands sold to homeowners, contractors and builders through major home-improvement retailers across Canada and the United States. Its head office and manufacturing are in Mississauga.
The business is in a strong growth phase. It aims to double in size over the next five years, and U.S. sales recently passed Canadian sales for the first time. It is investing heavily in automation and vertical integration, and it is actively exploring acquisitions. It is Great Place To Work® Certified.

The Opportunity

The Director of Finance will lead the finance function, sit on the leadership team and report directly to the Managing Director. The owners want to hand over day-to-day financial oversight, and this is a newly dedicated leadership role with full ownership of finance. The Managing Director is looking for a true right-hand partner: someone who will challenge assumptions, bring financial discipline to growth decisions and help steer the business. The role is also part of the company’s longer-term succession planning for senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Finance Leadership & Team Development
Lead all aspects of the finance function, including accounting, reporting, planning, cash management and financial governance.
Lead a team of two direct reports and assess whether the function’s structure and capability will support continued growth.
Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Managing Director and shareholders.

Financial Reporting & Governance
Oversee accurate, timely monthly reporting for the Canadian and U.S. entities, including consolidated results.
Prepare the monthly shareholder reporting package and support board-level reporting.
Lead the year-end close and audit, and maintain sound accounting policies and internal controls.
Coordinate tax compliance and planning with external advisors across Canada and the U.S.

Costing, Planning & Decision Support
Develop product costing, cost-per-unit and margin analysis in partnership with plant and operations leadership.
Build profitability reporting by product, customer, channel and region to support pricing and commercial decisions.
Lead the annual budget, a rolling 12-month forecast that integrates cash flow and covenant compliance, and longer-range planning.
Build business cases for key decisions and evaluate capital investment in equipment, automation and capacity.

Banking, Cash & Risk
Lead cash-flow planning and working capital management and, over time, take on responsibility for the lender relationships.
Manage foreign exchange exposure and oversee the insurance program.

Reporting, Systems & Automation
Enhance the KPIs and Power BI dashboards built on Business Central.
Work with IT to further automate finance processes and build AI fluency across the finance team, while keeping strong controls in place.

M&A & Strategic Initiatives
Support acquisitions through financial modelling, due diligence and valuation analysis.
Lead the financial integration of acquired businesses, covering reporting, systems, processes and controls.

The Ideal Candidate

CPA designation, with progressive finance experience in manufacturing and currently in a senior finance leadership role.
Hands-on expertise in costing, manufacturing economics, budgeting, forecasting and management reporting.
Experience in an owner-managed or entrepreneurial environment, working closely with engaged, financially sophisticated owners and a lean team.
M&A and integration experience is a strong asset.
A motivated, competitive, forward-looking leader who wants to help build something: confident enough to challenge, willing to roll up their sleeves, and ready to grow into broader leadership responsibilities over time.

This is a full-time, on-site role based in Mississauga.

To learn more in confidence, please apply through LinkedIn
